tier_s_must_memorize_cold.fact: End-to-end managed: ingest → chunk → embed → index → retrieve. Native sources: S3, web crawler, Confluence, SharePoint, Salesforce, Atlassian. Default chunking ≈ 300 tokens, 20% overlap. Ingestion is NOT automatic — run StartIngestionJob (manual or EventBridge-scheduled). Picks when stem says 'reduce ops overhead' + 'ground with my data'.

1) Content filters (Hate/Insults/Sexual/Violence/Misconduct/Prompt-Attack — NONE/LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH, separate input+output)
2) Denied topics (natural-language subjects)
3) Word filters (custom blocklist + profanity)
4) Sensitive info (PII types + custom regex; DETECT/ANONYMIZE/BLOCK)
5) Contextual grounding (groundedness + relevance, 0-1 numeric)
6) Image content filter
Also usable standalone via ApplyGuardrail API.

Action group = (OpenAPI 3.0 schema OR Function Detail) + Lambda backing (OR Return Control to caller). Sessions persist via sessionId. 4 overridable prompt templates: Pre-Processing → Orchestration → KB Response Generation → Post-Processing. Native KB attachment (no Lambda glue needed for KB read).

tier_s_must_memorize_cold.topic: RAG vs Fine-tune vs Continued Pre-training
tier_s_must_memorize_cold.fact: Data CHANGES (weekly/daily) → RAG (Knowledge Bases). STYLE/TONE/FORMAT/TASK with labeled examples → Fine-tune. New DOMAIN VOCAB on UNLABELED corpora → Continued Pre-training. Custom (fine-tuned) models on Bedrock REQUIRE Provisioned Throughput to host.

On-Demand: pay-per-token, no commit, regional, base FMs only. Provisioned Throughput: 1mo/6mo commit, Model Units = guaranteed capacity, REQUIRED for custom-model hosting. Batch: ~50% cheaper, async, ≤24h SLA, JSONL in/out in S3 — wrong for interactive.

ARN abstraction that routes invocation across multiple regions for resilience + capacity. System-defined (AWS-managed) vs Application (custom, tag-able for cost). Required for some newer model invocations. Quotas counted at the HOME region. Watch out: routing across regions can violate data residency.

OpenSearch Serverless vector: default for KBs, low-ops. Aurora pgvector: reuse existing Postgres. MemoryDB: single-digit-ms latency, Redis-compatible. DocumentDB elastic clusters: MongoDB-compatible, small scale. Neptune Analytics: graph + vector hybrid. Choose by latency, scale, existing-stack.

CloudTrail (control- and data-plane API metadata — who/when) + Model Invocation Logging (prompt + completion + metadata to S3 or CloudWatch) + Guardrail trace (which policy fired, in invocation logs) + Agent trace (rationale + tool calls + KB hits). Use ALL for full audit.

D1.fact: S3, web crawler, Confluence Cloud, SharePoint, Salesforce, Atlassian. Multiple sources can be combined in a single KB.
≈ 300 tokens per chunk with ~20% overlap. Override with Fixed, Semantic, or Hierarchical.
Default = quick start. Fixed = predictable size. Semantic = narrative grouping. Hierarchical = parent-child for long structured docs (manuals, legal).
Input: up to 8192 tokens. Output dims: 256 / 512 / 1024 (pick smaller = cheaper/faster ANN; larger = best accuracy).
Cohere Embed Multilingual v3 for cross-lingual. Cohere Embed English v3 for English-only. Titan Embed v2 = flexible dims. Titan Multimodal G1 = text + image SAME vector space.
AWS does NOT use customer prompts or completions for training base models — neither AWS-owned nor third-party. No opt-out needed because no use.
Not automatic. Use StartIngestionJob (manual or EventBridge scheduled). Common 'why isn't my new doc retrievable' gotcha.
MemoryDB (single-digit ms) < OpenSearch Serverless (tens of ms) < Aurora pgvector / DocumentDB. Pick MemoryDB only when sub-5ms is required.
Macie = AT REST in S3. Guardrails Sensitive Info = AT REQUEST TIME. Comprehend PII = NLP detection for custom pipelines. Use Macie + Guardrails together.
Sign BAA with AWS. Then use HIPAA-eligible services. Bedrock is HIPAA-eligible (most models). GovCloud is for ITAR/FedRAMP-High, NOT HIPAA.
Brings fine-tuned weights for SUPPORTED architectures (e.g., Llama, Mistral, Flan-T5) into Bedrock. Served via standard InvokeModel API.
Replicate the SOURCE (S3 Cross-Region Replication) and recreate or re-sync the KB in the DR region. Cross-region INFERENCE routes traffic, not data.

D2.fact: FM decides next step → Agents. Deterministic predefined workflow → Step Functions. If the stem says 'LLM picks the tool', it's Agents.
Two styles: OpenAPI 3.0 schema OR Function Detail (name + parameters inline). Function Detail is simpler when you don't already have an OpenAPI spec.
Agent returns tool-call details to the calling application; the app executes (not a Lambda action group). Use when execution must stay inside the existing app.
InvokeModelWithResponseStream returns chunks for interactive UIs. InvokeModel is non-streaming. InvokeAgent supports streaming events for Agents.
Claude 3 family (Sonnet/Opus/Haiku) and Amazon Nova Lite/Pro/Premier are vision-capable for image UNDERSTANDING. Generation = Titan Image, SDXL, Nova Canvas, Nova Reel (video).
Input/Output, Prompt, Knowledge Base, Agent, Lambda, Condition (branching), Iterator (loops). Visual GenAI orchestration, lower-code than Step Functions.
Native supervisor + specialist sub-agents pattern on Bedrock. Routes tasks, aggregates results. Use when scenario says 'agent of agents' or 'supervisor + specialists'.
Pre-Processing → Orchestration (with KB/Action calls in a ReAct loop) → Post-Processing → Response. Each has an overridable prompt template.
temperature ≈ 0 + top_p ≈ 1 for most reproducible output. Higher temperature = creative, NOT more accurate.
Few-shot exemplars → format consistency. Chain-of-Thought ('think step by step') → multi-step reasoning accuracy. Combine for best results.
Lambda needs a resource-based policy granting bedrock.amazonaws.com permission to invoke it, scoped to the Agent ARN. Forgetting this = most common Agent action failure.
Anthropic Claude Tool Use (Function Calling) via the Messages API: pass `tools`, model returns tool_use, app executes, returns tool_result. Works without spinning up a full Agent.

D3.fact: Six: Content filters | Denied topics | Word filters | Sensitive info (PII) | Contextual grounding | Image content. Plus standalone ApplyGuardrail API.
Per category, per direction (input/output), four levels: NONE / LOW / MEDIUM / HIGH. HIGH = block aggressively. Distinct from Contextual Grounding which is numeric 0-1.
Two numeric thresholds: groundedness (response supported by retrieved context) + relevance (retrieved context relevant to query). Both 0-1. The runtime hallucination defense.
Use Content filter category PROMPT ATTACK on the INPUT side. Detects jailbreaks/injections. Don't try to handcraft a word filter for this.
Scope bedrock:InvokeModel to a specific foundation-model ARN: arn:aws:bedrock:REGION::foundation-model/MODEL_ID. User-Agent / IP conditions are weak controls.
Per account, per region, manual enablement on Bedrock Model Access page — required BEFORE IAM can authorize. AccessDenied on new accounts usually = missing Model Access.
Customer-managed KMS keys (CMK) supported for: model invocation logs, custom model artifacts, KB ingested data, Agent/Prompt resources.
Four: bedrock (control), bedrock-runtime (data — InvokeModel), bedrock-agent (control — Agents), bedrock-agent-runtime (data — InvokeAgent). NAT Gateway is NOT private.
Third-party model providers (Anthropic, Cohere, Meta, Mistral, etc.) do NOT access customer prompts/completions when invoked through Bedrock.

CloudTrail = WHO called WHAT API WHEN. Model invocation logging = full PROMPT/COMPLETION. Guardrail trace = which policy fired. Agent trace = FM rationale + tool calls. Use the right layer for the question.
SageMaker Clarify for fine-tuned and custom models — pre/post-training bias metrics, SHAP feature attribution. Bedrock Model Evaluation can include fairness criteria.
Service Control Policies (SCPs) on an OU deny bedrock:InvokeModel on specific model ARNs — overrides any IAM in member accounts. Config detects; SCPs PREVENT.

D4.fact: Sporadic/low → On-Demand. Steady high → Provisioned Throughput (1mo/6mo). Offline bulk → Batch (~50% off, ≤24h).
Fine-tuned (custom) models REQUIRE Provisioned Throughput to host on Bedrock. On-Demand is only for base FMs.
5-minute TTL. Cache WRITE ≈ 1.25× base input. Cache READ ≈ 0.1× base input. Break-even ≈ 2–3 reuses within TTL. Supported on Claude (cache_control breakpoints on system/tools/messages).
Highest-ROI cost lever. Haiku / Nova Micro for high-volume light. Sonnet / Nova Pro for balanced. Opus / Nova Premier for deep reasoning. Try smaller first.
Provision PT for the BASELINE; let On-Demand absorb peaks. Provisioning for peak is the classic over-commit mistake.
JSONL in S3 → CreateModelInvocationJob → JSONL out in S3. Async, ≤24h SLA, ~50% discount vs On-Demand.
1) Backoff with jitter, 2) Service Quotas TPM/RPM increase, 3) Cross-region inference profile, 4) Provisioned Throughput for sustained loads.
Cross-region inference profile routes to multiple regions for capacity/resilience while keeping caller in one home region. Quotas counted at the home region.
AWS Budgets = threshold alerts (fixed $). AWS Cost Anomaly Detection = ML-based unexpected-pattern alerts. Cost Explorer = analysis (no alerting).
Tag-able profiles for cost allocation across teams/products. Tags propagate to Cost Explorer + AWS Budgets. Different from system-defined cross-region inference profiles.
Output CAP, not the actual output length. Reducing it doesn't reduce latency by itself.

D5.fact: Automated (built-in datasets + standard metrics like BLEU/ROUGE/F1). Human (your in-house team, custom criteria). LLM-as-a-Judge (FM scores subjective quality at scale, cheaper than human).
Translation → BLEU. Summarization → ROUGE (1/2/L). Semantic similarity → BERTScore. Classification → F1, Accuracy. QA exact match → EM. LM uncertainty → Perplexity. Image gen → FID/CLIPScore.
Recall@K (gold in top-K?), Precision@K (relevant fraction), MRR (rank of first relevant), NDCG (graded relevance with position discount), Hit Rate. For RAG retrieval evaluation.
Invocations, InputTokenCount, OutputTokenCount, InvocationLatency, InvocationThrottles, InvocationClientErrors, InvocationServerErrors. Dimension by model.
Runtime: Guardrails Contextual Grounding (auto-block ungrounded). Offline: RAGAS framework. Combined with RAG + lower temperature for best results.
Shadow = mirror, zero user impact. Canary = % to new variant, small user impact. Blue/green = atomic cutover. Pick by user-impact tolerance.
SageMaker Model Monitor handles 4 drift types: data quality, model quality, bias, feature attribution. For Bedrock-only GenAI, build custom CloudWatch metrics + scheduled Evaluation jobs.
EventBridge schedule → Lambda orchestrator → Bedrock Model Evaluation job → S3 results bucket → Athena + QuickSight dashboards.
Agent trace = FM rationale + tool calls + KB retrievals per InvokeAgent. Captured in model invocation logs when enabled.
Guardrail traces are emitted inside model invocation logs (S3 or CloudWatch) — not a separate log product. Query via Athena or CloudWatch Logs Insights.
Truncate / chunk long inputs + retrieve only top-K via RAG + pre-validate token count client-side. max_tokens is OUTPUT cap, not input window.
Check: cross-region inference health, region of execution, network path (PrivateLink vs internet), model version changes, prompt-size drift, downstream Lambda cold-starts.
